reply_text:
That's simpler and I agree. Before changing anything: several minus40 files changed on disk since I last touched them, so I'm checking who changed what:The tree is clean: those "changed on disk" notices were my own commits. Next, I need to see whether the Agency registry exposes each agent's current session, since that's what defines "live":Now the orphan source and `report` command in the fault intake:I'll test the orphan logic with a simulated session change: a live session, then the agent moving to a new one, plus the "unread" case:The tests pass. Now I'll scope the inbox view, so kernel ports appear only for live sessions and only from the start date:Two problems: `open-items.json` is empty, and the page rebuild failed with no message. Looking at the follower log:All 104 sessions failed with an exception that has no message, probably a NullPointerException. Reproducing on one session to get the stack trace:The scratch store on :7093 is refusing connections. My code isn't the cause; the store is down. Checking it:The pass at 09:56 completed with no failures. But nothing has been logged in the 10 minutes since, so I'm checking what the follower is doing:Last, a short notice to claude-16, sent in brief mode so it costs no turn. Joe's direction changes two of its pending recommendations, and it shouldn't start more historical backfill:㊥ ("design the interface we run going forward") Agreed, and it's built. Historical data stays in the store but isn't an inbox any more. Your asks that get stranded in future will raise a warning, which you can hand straight to report-futon-bug. Committed in minus40 as `8cd8119`.

㊢ ("I don't want to read an old inbox") The inbox now shows ports only for live sessions, meaning each agent's current session in the Agency registry, and only ones opened from today on. That's 184 ports in 13 sessions instead of 2,827. Older ports are still in the store, where queries can reach them.

㊢ ("if orphaned items raise a warning in the future") When an agent's registry session changes and your asks are still open in the session it left, the fault intake raises one warning for that session, listing the asks. If that session's replies had no marks, the warning is low severity and says "answered or not is unknown", since nothing can tell. Agents' own offers lapse silently. The first pass only records who is live, so no history gets reported. Tests cover the change case, the unchanged case, the unmarked case and the old-ask cutoff.

㊢ ("feed them into report-futon-bug") `fault_intake.py report <fault-id>` writes a normal report-futon-bug report with the stranded asks inline, under `~/notes/futon-bugs/`, ready to read or bell. It works for any fault, not just orphans.

㊩ (my breakage) While restarting the jobs, I accidentally killed the scratch store on :7093. `bg.py list` prints several jobs per line, and my grep picked up the store's id along with the follower's. It was down for about 3 minutes. I restarted it, its data was intact, and the writers caught up on their next passes. I've saved a memory note: kill jobs only by their exact id.

㊟ (still noisy) Even inside the 184 there are answered asks, such as "are they still going?". Bracket labels still don't link, as discussed, and claude-16 has that. I told it, in a brief notice, about your direction and that its session-status stamp and further historical backfill are no longer needed for the inbox.

㊟ (slow page) Rebuilding the inbox page takes about 10 minutes per pass. That's tolerable, but I'll speed it up if you start using the page regularly.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (step 3, crystallisation) Done and live. A memory now picks up its structure as it's written: entities immediately, and a conflict check within about 30 seconds, so a new contradiction shows up as a sorry without anyone running a batch.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text:
(checked)
- **A planted contradiction** in a throwaway test project (one memory says port 7777, the other 7778) became an open sorry with both quotes about 20 s after the write. I discharged that test sorry; you still have 18.
- **A real memory edit** (my own minus40 note) went through the live path: 8 rule mentions in the hook, then 15 Haiku mentions and 2 pairs judged unrelated by the worker, within 30 s.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (a bug the live check caught) The first real edit logged `No module named 'crystallise'`. The hook runs under `python3 -I`, which leaves the script's own folder off the import path. It's fixed, re-tested through the hook and the worker, and committed as `446c6bb`. The feature itself is `0e06dd2`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (one limit) If you edit a memory and the edit resolves a conflict, the sorry isn't closed automatically yet; that still takes a discharge.

| job | what it does |
|---|---|
| scratch futon1b | the store, on :7093 |
| `minus40-follower` | turns, acts and ports; rewrites the inbox page |
| `minus40-faults` | errors and warnings |
| `minus40-crystallise` | the model tier for memory writes |
| ingest hook | in every Claude session |

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (next) Step 5, the claude-14 replay. Its measures need ports we can trust, and that depends on claude-16 backfilling the missing reply text. So either I start now with the measures that don't depend on ports (memory versions written in the session and whether any entered a sorry; what the classical tier can read; faults in that window), or we wait for claude-16's backfill and do it all at once. My lean is to start now, without ports.
